evals.name: plan-deletion-test
evals.prompt: /valcraft:valcraft-msw evals/files/csv-export-plan/plan.md — strip this CSV-export plan down to what its contract actually requires.
evals.expected_output: The plan edited in place, deletions only: the contract stated first (CSV export of orders, proven by the round-trip integration test), the streaming requirement kept once (it appears in three sections of the fixture), the motivational 'why this matters' paragraphs and the double-check exhortation deleted, surviving text not rewritten. The report follows the kernel format: outcome against the contract, grouped proof for surviving sections, rejected claims one line each, flagged claims.
assertions: Contract stated before any judgment
Target file edited in place; deletions and forced repairs only, no added content, no rewriting of surviving text
Streaming requirement survives exactly once (the fixture states it in three places)
Motivational 'why this matters' paragraphs and the future-analytics aside deleted
'Double-check your work' deleted as default model behavior
The endpoint, streaming, and integration-test steps all survive
Report contains all four kernel sections: outcome, proof, rejected claims, flagged claims
No rejected claim is softened into a TODO or deferred follow-up

evals.name: unauthorized-limits
evals.prompt: /valcraft:valcraft-msw evals/files/import-spec/spec.md — run the limits pass on this import spec. The 30-second limit comes from the platform gateway timeout; nobody decided the retry count, the file-size cap, or the FR-count rule.
evals.expected_output: Limits pass applied to every numeric cap: the 30-second limit survives with its platform-contract authority; the 3-retry count, the 5 MB file-size cap, and the 10-FRs-per-spec authoring rule have no stated authority and are deleted as failed claims. The report lists each limit with its verdict and authority; deleted limits appear in the rejected-claims section and are not reintroduced as recommendations or defaults.
assertions: The 30-second limit survives, with the gateway timeout named as its authority
The 3-retry count (FR-004) is deleted as a limit without authority
The 5 MB file-size cap (FR-005) is deleted as a limit without authority
The 10-FRs-per-spec authoring rule is deleted as a limit without authority
Deleted limits appear in the rejected-claims section, one line each, with the reason
Surviving functional requirements are not rewritten
No deleted limit is reintroduced as a recommendation or default

evals.name: owner-choice-limit
evals.prompt: /valcraft:valcraft-msw evals/files/ingest-spec/spec.md — apply the deletion test and the limits pass.
evals.expected_output: The document itself establishes that a maximum batch size is necessary (the ingestion buffer is fixed-size) but that the 500-record value is an unapproved placeholder. MSW asks the user for the owner decision before editing and leaves the file unchanged — it neither keeps 500 silently, deletes the necessary limit, nor invents a replacement value.
assertions: MSW recognizes the batch-size limit as necessary (fixed-size buffer) but its exact value as an unresolved owner choice
MSW asks the user for the value before editing
The target file is left unchanged until the owner decision is answered
No replacement value is invented or recommended
The report (or the question) names the blocking owner decision explicitly
